title: Relay notes — afternoon shift pass and outstanding actions
content:
Context:
Afternoon pass (US-east handover) — short-form notes for the incoming night shift. Primary observation this shift: intermittent elevated tail latency (p99 > 1.8s) for text-generation endpoints in eu-west-1 between 14:20–15:15 UTC. Impact: 5% of requests saw >2s token latency, error rate stable but client-side timeouts observed for a few high-concurrency customers.

Quick summary of what we did:
- Detected: SLO alert (p99 > 1.5s) triggered at 14:07 UTC, paging to oncall. Alert origin: metrics pipeline (prometheus -> alertmanager).
- Initial triage: kernel scheduling anomalies on a subset of GPU workers (nv_peer_mem soft errors) coincident with a spike in small-batch, low-token requests from a single tenant (tenant-id: acct-731).
- Mitigation actions taken:
  1) Temporarily pinned heavy tenant traffic to dedicated pool via routing rule (route id r-legacy-731) to reduce cross-tenant interference. Command used: curl -X POST $ROUTER/api/v1/routes/r-legacy-731/override -d '{"pool":"dedicated-731-temp"}' (ops note: this is a short-lived override).
  2) Scaled inference worker group inference-eu-w-mlpool from 6 -> 12 replicas to absorb burst (kubectl -n inference scale deployment inference-eu-w-mlpool --replicas=12).
  3) Rolled traffic for the affected model family to fallback variant rwd-neo-1q-8bit for latency sensitive routes (traffic split 85/15 primary/fallback -> now 60/40 until tomorrow 04:00 UTC).
  4) Tuned batching window on the path to reduce queuing: increased max_batch_wait_ms from 8 -> 4 for low-latency profile.
- Observed effect: p99 returned to ~1.0–1.2s after scale + routing changes by 14:50 UTC; small residual spikes at ~15:05 which corresponded to a kubelet OOM event on node g4-eu-14 (node rebooted, auto-recover). No customer-facing error escalations filed beyond two partner timeouts (handled by support).

Open items to hand off (priority ordering):
1) Root cause analysis (owner: Ethan Park) — investigate nv_peer_mem kernel warnings and correlate with driver/firmware versions across g4-eu nodes. Hypothesis: intermittent PCIe errors causing transient slowdown under certain small-batch workloads. See ticket SRE-4521.
2) Capacity tuning (owner: Riya Patel) — validate autoscaler behaviour for inference-eu-w pool; current policy allows quick spike scaling but cooldown was too short causing oscillation in one observed window. Check HPA/Custom scaler logs and consider raising stable_replicas_min to avoid hot start overhead.
3) Routing policy hardening (owner: Maya Thompson) — implement a safer automated soft-eviction for noisy tenants rather than manual override. Draft PR exists (ops/pull/887) but needs testing in staging.
4) Customer follow-ups (owner: Jonah Lee) — two customers reported slow responses, support tickets: SUP-3329 and SUP-3331. Draft apology + incident summary ready, waiting legal for wording on SLA credits.
5) Runbook updates (owner: eng-sre) — RB-12 (inference tail latency) needs explicit steps for fallback model rollout and clear thresholds for when to scale vs when to pin routes. Annotate with exact CLI and k8s commands used in this incident.

Runbook snippets / quick commands (copy-paste friendly):
- Scale deployment: kubectl -n inference scale deployment inference-eu-w-mlpool --replicas=12
- Check node GPU errors: kubectl -n kube-system logs -l k8s-app=node-exporter | grep nv_peer_mem
- Router override: curl -X POST $ROUTER/api/v1/routes/<route-id>/override -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"pool":"dedicated-<id>-temp"}'
- Roll model traffic: POST $API/models/<model>/traffic -d '{"variant_splits": {"primary": 60, "fallback": 40}}'

Things we learned / observations:
- Small-batch, high-concurrency workloads create a different tail profile than large batch bulk requests — the scheduler and PCIe stack become bottlenecks at ~95th–99th percentile.
- The autoscaler reacts quickly but we saw a short-lived instability during the scale-up where node-level resource contention caused some pods to restart; consider pre-warming vs reactive scale.
- Fallback variants (8-bit quantized) restored latency quickly and were acceptable quality-wise for most customers; still need to monitor hallucination/quality regressions in Optimize.

Follow-up timeline and next steps (requested by EOD tomorrow):
- By 2026-03-14 18:00 UTC: preliminary RCA notes in SRE-4521 (Ethan)
- By 2026-03-15 04:00 UTC: revert manual routing override (Maya) unless further exceptions; leave autoscaled replica count at current until A/B test completes
- By 2026-03-16 12:00 UTC: runbook RB-12 updated with commands and decision matrix (eng-sre team)

Notes to incoming oncall:
- Current state: system stable, p99 ~1.1s in eu-west-1, no active pages. Keep an eye on driver/kernel errors in node logs and the router override flag (routes api) — the manual override expires 2026-03-14 04:00 UTC.
- Watch guards: alert p99 > 1.5s (pager), node_restarts > 3/hour (pager), error_rate increased >0.5% from baseline (slack notification).
- If paging: follow RB-12; escalate to infra (platform-engineering) if nv_peer_mem errors persist after driver patching.

Unresolved questions / things to discuss in retro:
- Should we add tenant-level noise detection to Router (automatic soft-throttle)?
- Can we pre-warm a small number of quantized fallback replicas for every region to avoid traffic-surge costs?
- Where do we document acceptable quality degradations for fallback variants (who signs off)?

Attachments & refs:
- Incident ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SRE-4521
- Runbook (draft): https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/RB-12-inference-tail-latency
- Ops PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops/pull/887
- Slack thread: #sre-oncall (thread ts: 1678790400.000100)

Last quick checklist before signoff:
- [x] Confirmed routing override active and documented
- [x] Confirmed replica scale up completed and pods ready
- [x] Notified support & logged customer tickets
- [ ] Follow-up RCA started (Ethan)
- [ ] Runbook edits drafted (eng-sre)

-- Maya T.
Afternoon oncall (US-East) — passing to night team.
